properties.chose: (a), kept by Anthony on 2026-10-10 as req:a-design-takes-a-chunk-of-another-as-copies-with-provenance-and-a-watch: one call copies a shown chunk into the taker, each node imported from the source, linked back to its origin, proposed until accepted, and upstream_status reports when an origin moves. (b) reference-only was not taken because the taker's own checks could not see the chunk; (c) live inheritance stays considered as the larger build for when a taker wants to follow the source. (d) by hand is what StoryFlow did today.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-10: "may also be worth implementing something like: add oauth key:values from flo2 to storyflow. Then storyflow doesn't have to retrieve how to do oauth properly, it can just inherit from flo2's implementation. This is one example, but having one design just take 'chunks' of another design would be cool."

WHAT EXISTS: a requirement travels between designs one at a time: receive_from_design in the taker (as moved, piece or derived, provenance imported, source the far design, proposed until accepted) and send_to_design in the giver, each side its own write (slice 3, 0.81.0). A typed reference (xref) stands in for a far node and is checked by upstream_status when the far design moves. import_graph layers a whole export onto a design under the original ids (and would overwrite on a different design: compose.rs's warning). compose_and_analyse assembles under namespaces for a question and writes nothing. What StoryFlow did today by hand, four requirements rewritten from flo2's, is a chunk taken as a copy with prose citations, now with typed links.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) A CHUNK AS A COPY WITH PROVENANCE: `take_from_design` (or receive_from_design widened) takes a topic neighbourhood from the source, one call, and writes each node into the taker with provenance imported, source the far design, and an xref back to its origin, every one proposed until the taker's owner accepts. The taker owns the copies and may reword them; upstream_status reports when an origin moved, so the taker can look. MEDIUM: the chunk boundary is the hard part (a topic neighbourhood, or a region from a seed and depth, as claim_region computes), and ids must be renamed or namespaced to avoid colliding with the taker's own.
(b) A CHUNK AS A REFERENCE: no copy; the taker holds xref references to the chunk's nodes and reads them through the far design when asked (the assembled-when-asked machinery). Nothing to keep in step; nothing the taker can reword; and nothing in the taker for its own checks to see (a capability in StoryFlow cannot SATISFY a requirement that lives in flo2).
(c) LIVE INHERITANCE: the taker's copies follow the source's changes (a pull, with a diff shown, accepted or refused per node), so StoryFlow's OAuth stays in step with flo2's unless StoryFlow diverges on purpose. The largest: it is a merge of a subgraph across designs, which cap:merge-designs does for whole designs under one id space.
(d) BY HAND, as today: read, rewrite, link.

PUSHBACK, KEPT BESIDE IT:
- A COPY IS A FORK. The one-home rule (a fact has one home; the hub reads it by reference) exists because copies drift. (a) makes the drift visible (upstream_status) rather than preventing it; (c) prevents it at the cost of a merge.
- A CHUNK HAS NO NATURAL EDGE. "flo2's OAuth" is a topic, not a node: its boundary is a judgement (the four nodes StoryFlow took, or the twelve a topic walk finds). The call must show the chunk before writing it.
- TWO OWNERS. The source's owner wrote the chunk for their design; taking it into another credits the taker and marks it imported, as receive_from_design does; the origin's authorship stays visible through the xref.
- INHERITANCE WITHOUT A CONTRACT IS NOT INHERITANCE. In code, inheriting means the base can change under you; here (a) gives a snapshot with a watch, which is what most takers want, and (c) gives the real thing, which few will accept node by node.
- CHEAPEST: (a) is receive_from_design in bulk plus a boundary; it reuses provenance, xref and upstream_status as they are.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-10 — a design takes a chunk of another as copies with provenance and a watch (option a); reference-only and live inheritance stay considered
